item.title: At G20 Summit, Some U.S. Allies Push Back on Trump’s Economic Approach
item.description: At a summit meant to showcase President Trump’s economic policies as a model for the world, Europeans complained about tariffs and the war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Jim Tankersley
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, left, and the Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin M. Warsh, met with Group of 20 finance ministers and central banker governors on Tuesday in Asheville, N.C.

item.title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?

item.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
item.description: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.media:credit: Morgan Lieberman for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. employers are bracing for what looks to be the sharpest increase in health care costs in more than two decades.

item.media:description: Russia has turned to a terrifying new tactic in its assaults on Ukraine, launching nonstop waves of armed drones into busy areas of Kyiv.

item.title: Six Takeaways From the Massachusetts Primaries
item.description: Senator Ed Markey, 80, trounced a younger challenger who had made an argument for generational change. Two other longtime Democratic lawmakers hung on, too.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:description: Senator Ed Markey, who has served in Washington for 50 years, easily beat back a challenge from a younger Democrat.

item.title: Billionaires Sent Montana Prices Soaring. Can Democrats Capitalize?
item.description: For years, Democrats have failed to harness the anger of Montanans contending with out-of-state wealth driving up costs. This year, a smokejumper thinks he can succeed.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sam Forstag, a telegenic firefighter and union leader, is the Democratic candidate for a House race in Montana.

item.title: Woman Killed in Times Square Stabbing Identified as Bank of America VP
item.description: The New York Police Department is still trying to piece together what led a 49-year-old woman to stab two strangers, one fatally.
item.dc:creator: Maria Cramer, Chelsia Rose Marcius and Mark Bonamo
item.media:description: A knife-wielding 49-year-old woman attacked two people in Times Square before she was shot and fatally wounded by the police.

item.title: ‘Don’t Worry About Me’: Attacker’s Father Thought She Had Turned a Corner
item.description: Pamela Cisneros was killed by the police in Times Square after she stabbed two people, one fatally. Her father said she had stopped going with him to her mental health appointments.
item.dc:creator: Chelsia Rose Marcius, Miles G. Cohen, Amy Julia Harris and Katelyn Ferral
item.media:description: Pamela Cisneros fatally stabbed a 32-year-old woman and wounded a 68-year-old man in Times Square on Monday, the police said.

item.title: Times Square Police Shooting Was Justified but Put Others at Risk, Experts Say
item.description: Officers who stood around a woman wielding two kitchen knives, and then opened fire without clearing the area, risked harming themselves or passers-by, the experts said.
item.dc:creator: Andy Newman
item.media:description: The police said a woman stabbed two people in Times Square on Monday, killing a 32-year-old woman.

item.title: The ‘Miracle House’ That Survived Nepal’s Floods

item.title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
item.description: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: North American Blue Energy Partners Inc
item.media:description: Oil infrastructure in Cabimas, Venezuela. Chevron’s expansion is separate from President Trump’s deal for control of oil reserves in the country.

item.title: A.I. Is to Be Banned in N.Y.C. Elementary and Middle Schools
item.description: A new policy to be announced by the Department of Education bars younger students from using artificial intelligence, but stops short of a moratorium.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haag
item.media:credit: Sara Messinger for The New York Times

item.title: Attacks in Black Sea Threaten to Strangle Global Grain Supply
item.description: Strikes on ports and vessels by both Russia and Ukraine have left farmers facing ruin and could cause another worldwide food shock.

item.media:credit: Jędrzej Nowicki for The New York Times
item.media:description: A field in Ukraine’s southern region of Mykolvaiv in August. Despite a strong growing season, attacks on Black Sea shipping routes have choked off exports.

item.title: These Ukrainian Children Go to School Underground. They’re the Lucky Ones.

item.media:description: The first day of school at Sichovy Collegium in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Tuesday. The school operates from an underground space, built to allow children to continue learning safely amid the war.
